title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US equity futures fell (Nasdaq 100 -1%+, S&P 500 -0.6%) after AI industry leaders called for a development slowdown, reversing Friday's rebound (S&P had snapped a 4-day losing streak, +0.9%).
Markets: Brent crude spiked back above $108/bbl (highest since May), reversing the weekend's easing, as Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut after fresh drone strikes launched from Iraq.

Companies: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman jointly urged slowing AI development over safety risks; Elon Musk backed the call, following a high-profile ex-Anthropic researcher's resignation warning of a reckless race to superintelligence.

Companies: Nvidia is reportedly weighing a ~$10B investment in Anthropic's expected IPO (targeting ~$100B raise at a ~$2T valuation); Dell extended gains on strong earnings while Oracle's post-earnings pop reversed into a roughly 2% decline.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's FOMC meets Sept 15-16 with a rate decision Wednesday, finely balanced between a hold and a hike after hot August CPI (3.4% Y/Y, core +0.3% M/M) and strong payrolls under new hawkish Chair Kevin Warsh.

Macro/Policy: Iraq blamed drone launches from Maysan province (near the Iran border) for the Saudi pipeline attack, dismissed a military commander, and launched an investigation as Gulf states plan Hormuz-security talks with Iran in Oman this week.
